questions.key_step: Test each property on a 5-pair relation: (2,3) in R but (3,2) is not.
questions.justification: Single direct counter-example on a tiny relation; same one-move demand as 2026-P1-Q3 (L1).

questions.key_step: Read R as divisibility; reflexive and transitive but (6,12) has no reverse.
questions.justification: Eight pairs to scan for transitivity, otherwise routine; one familiar idea (divisibility order).

questions.key_step: Words sharing a letter: BAD-CAT-KITE chain breaks transitivity.
questions.justification: One familiar counter-example; needs only the idea of constructing a chain.

questions.key_step: S fails reflexivity (x=x+1 impossible); T is 'x-y integer', a standard equivalence.
questions.justification: Two standard checks, each one move; equivalence-relation question so +0.5.

questions.key_step: Element chase: x in B gives x in C using both intersection and union equalities.
questions.justification: Known cancellation law for sets; one idea, no computation.

questions.key_step: The zero real number breaks symmetry of 'x = wy'; S is equality of fractions.
questions.justification: Two relations, hidden w=0 trap and the p=0 case in the transitivity of S; chain of routine checks, no new idea.

questions.key_step: y-x integer is an equivalence; x = alpha y fails symmetry through alpha=0; then judge the explanation.
questions.justification: Two statements plus a judgement on explanation; same w=0 trap as Q6.

questions.key_step: Transitivity of similarity uses (QP)^-1 = P^-1 Q^-1, which is exactly Statement 2.
questions.justification: Three equivalence checks on matrices and the 'is it the explanation' judgement.

questions.key_step: Each element is in Y only, Z only or neither: 3^5.
questions.justification: Standard counting trick met in every set-theory chapter.

questions.key_step: |A x B| = 8; subsets with 3 or more elements = 2^8 minus those with 0, 1 or 2.
questions.justification: One familiar complement count.

questions.key_step: Put t = sqrt(x) and split on |t-3|; check each root against its case.
questions.justification: Modulus plus root substitution, two cases with validity checks; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Sum of B in 100..999 is 54650; the rest 54950 must come from a disjoint C of 100 terms.
questions.justification: Numerical answer; AP sums over a 3-digit window and a disjointness assumption; slip-prone but standard.

questions.key_step: Equivalence class of a point under 'same distance from O' is the circle through it.
questions.justification: Single recognition step; equivalence-class wording gives +0.5.

questions.key_step: Conjugation by P: identity, inverse and product give reflexive, symmetric, transitive.
questions.justification: Standard similarity relation; one idea, equivalence adjustment applies.

questions.key_step: A triple region exists whenever the overlap of two circles lies inside the third.
questions.justification: Needs careful reading of three diagrams; no calculation but easy to misjudge.

questions.key_step: Class of (4,3): all (4k,3k) in A x A; k = 1..7.
questions.justification: Equivalence class by direct listing; one step.

questions.key_step: Split at 0 and -4; test each root for its own interval; D<0 in the middle case.
questions.justification: Three cases with a discriminant and validity checks; routine.

questions.key_step: Factor into (x-y)(x+y)(x-3y); on N only x=y or x=3y; (3,1) breaks symmetry.
questions.justification: Factorisation plus counter-examples for two properties; equivalence wording gives +0.5.

questions.key_step: n(n-1) <= 10000 gives A = {1..100}; B - C = odd members of B = 6j+1.
questions.justification: Bound, parity filter and AP sum; numerical format but short.
Two-set inclusion-exclusion with a bound; routine.

questions.key_step: Show 0<|x-y|<=1 is not transitive (0, 0.8, 1.6); check the other three relations.
questions.justification: Four relations, each needing a genuine counter-example or proof.

questions.key_step: Reduce each modulus set to intervals, take the complement, count integers -2..5, then 2^8.
questions.justification: Several interval operations in a chain; routine.

questions.key_step: Write A, B as intervals and compare B-A with R-(-3,1); true set is R-(-3,3).
questions.justification: Four interval statements to check; routine.

questions.key_step: Both |a-b|<=13 and |a-b|!=13 fail transitivity; build chains 1,12,19 and 10,15,23.
questions.justification: Two relations, two constructed counter-examples; equivalence adjustment applies.

questions.key_step: The relation says 'x and y lie in the same block of the partition'.
questions.justification: Abstract notation but standard fact (partition = equivalence relation).

questions.key_step: gcd(n,45)=1 means not divisible by 3 or 5; inclusion-exclusion on sums of evens up to 200.
questions.justification: Numerical answer, four sums to get exactly right, no options to check.

questions.key_step: R1-R2 = pairs (p, p^n) with n>=2: 4+2+1+1 = 8 prime powers.
questions.justification: Careful enumeration of prime powers up to 50; PDF itself slipped on the count of primes.

questions.key_step: ab>=0 fails transitivity through 0 (2,0,-2); a>=b is not symmetric.
questions.justification: Two quick counter-examples; equivalence adjustment applies.

questions.key_step: Reflexivity at x=1 forces 7 | 3+alpha; verify that this also gives symmetry and transitivity.
questions.justification: Necessary-and-sufficient reasoning with a parameter and remainders; slightly more abstract than the other relation questions.

questions.key_step: Distinct odd semiprimes up to 60 are 11; each b pairs with all 60 a's.
questions.justification: Count distinct products carefully (3x5 = 5x3), then multiply.

questions.key_step: Complement: subsets with 1 in, 2 out and non-prime sum; count by size from {3..7}.
questions.justification: No options; complement formulation plus prime checks on 32 sums, one slip changes the answer.

questions.key_step: Subsets meeting B = all subsets minus those inside A - B: 128 - 16.
questions.justification: Single familiar complement count.

questions.key_step: Evens >= 4 come from 4s and 6s; odds come from 9 plus an even; only 11 fails.
questions.justification: Needs the representability idea (4,6,9 combinations) and a clean proof; no options.

questions.key_step: Shift to the ellipse centre and count lattice points row by row inside both curves.
questions.justification: Lattice counting with two conics, strict natural-number restriction and no options; high slip risk.
